say: An electric car just broke five hundred kilometers an hour.
Why is five hundred so hard?
Air. Drag grows with speed squared.
Power to beat it grows with speed cubed.
Four hundred to five hundred? Nearly double the power.
Its answer: four motors, two point two megawatts.
The catch is heat, so temperatures were set before every run.
One percent faster costs about three percent more power.
And it was one way, not a two-way average.
